fact_text: Pakistan's Auto Policy 2026-31 was approved by the prime minister after the previous policy expired on 30 June 2026, but still needed clearance from the IMF, the Economic Coordination Committee and the cabinet.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'What Auto Policy 2026-31 Means for You (Jobs, Prices & Economy) Shafy's Weekly' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The Auto Policy 2026-31 draft projects cumulative foreign-exchange savings of 17.7 billion dollars from localised assembly, about 4.6 billion dollars of auto-part exports over five years and a net fiscal surplus near 21 billion dollars.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'What Auto Policy 2026-31 Means for You (Jobs, Prices & Economy) Shafy's Weekly' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The policy aims to protect the roughly 2.5 million jobs the analyst attributes to Pakistan's auto value chain.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'What Auto Policy 2026-31 Means for You (Jobs, Prices & Economy) Shafy's Weekly' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Under the draft policy, customs duty on imported built-up cars falls gradually to 2030-31 towards 35% up to 850cc, 40% for 850-1000cc, 45% for 1000-1500cc, 77% for 1500-1800cc and 115% above 1800cc.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'What Auto Policy 2026-31 Means for You (Jobs, Prices & Economy) Shafy's Weekly' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Regulatory and additional customs duties on imported cars are to be eliminated entirely by 2031 under the draft auto policy, which removes a layer of protection for local assemblers.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'What Auto Policy 2026-31 Means for You (Jobs, Prices & Economy) Shafy's Weekly' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The draft auto policy sets knocked-down import duty at 10% for non-localised parts and 15% for localised parts, while duty on raw materials is removed altogether.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'What Auto Policy 2026-31 Means for You (Jobs, Prices & Economy) Shafy's Weekly' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The draft policy earmarks about PKR 100 billion of direct subsidy for green vehicles, funded by a levy of 1% to 3% on internal-combustion cars, so petrol and diesel buyers cross-subsidise electric ones.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'What Auto Policy 2026-31 Means for You (Jobs, Prices & Economy) Shafy's Weekly' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Commercial imports of cars up to five years old would be allowed only for corporate tax filers with 3S dealer networks, with a 40% regulatory tariff that phases out by 2030.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'What Auto Policy 2026-31 Means for You (Jobs, Prices & Economy) Shafy's Weekly' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Pakistan's New Energy Vehicle Policy 2025-30 targets a 30% share of new vehicle sales for new energy vehicles by 2030, aiming to cut dependence on imported fuel.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'What Auto Policy 2026-31 Means for You (Jobs, Prices & Economy) Shafy's Weekly' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Pakistan imported roughly 16 billion dollars of petroleum in 2024, of which about 80% was consumed by the transport sector, which is why vehicle electrification is framed as a balance-of-payments policy.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'What Auto Policy 2026-31 Means for You (Jobs, Prices & Economy) Shafy's Weekly' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The New Energy Vehicle Policy is projected to deliver roughly PKR 730 billion of net economic benefit to Pakistan by 2030 through avoided fuel costs.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'What Auto Policy 2026-31 Means for You (Jobs, Prices & Economy) Shafy's Weekly' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The government caps refinery margins on diesel by allowing a fixed dollar margin over the actual landed cost of crude, and has cut that cap repeatedly, most recently from 41 dollars to 30 dollars per barrel during wartime conditions.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'What Auto Policy 2026-31 Means for You (Jobs, Prices & Economy) Shafy's Weekly' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: An earlier negotiated cut brought the diesel refinery margin down from above 50 dollars to 41 dollars per barrel, and that reduction passed straight through into a sharp fall in the retail diesel price.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'What Auto Policy 2026-31 Means for You (Jobs, Prices & Economy) Shafy's Weekly' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Because diesel margins are administratively set rather than market-determined, Pakistani refinery earnings carry recurring regulatory risk whenever the government wants to hold down pump prices.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'What Auto Policy 2026-31 Means for You (Jobs, Prices & Economy) Shafy's Weekly' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: For fiscal years 2026 and 2027 the government cut the additional customs duty on listed smartphones from 6% to 4% and reduced regulatory duty across the import-value slabs, with the largest cuts on phones above 500 dollars.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'What Auto Policy 2026-31 Means for You (Jobs, Prices & Economy) Shafy's Weekly' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Pakistan's mobile phone imports rose from 1.497 billion dollars in FY25 to 1.88 billion dollars in FY26.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'What Auto Policy 2026-31 Means for You (Jobs, Prices & Economy) Shafy's Weekly' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Currency in circulation in Pakistan rose by about PKR 1.8 trillion in FY2026 to roughly PKR 12.66 trillion.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'What Auto Policy 2026-31 Means for You (Jobs, Prices & Economy) Shafy's Weekly' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The State Bank spent about PKR 29.6 billion printing currency notes in FY2026 against PKR 27.8 billion the year before, a roughly 6% rise driven by growing currency in circulation.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'What Auto Policy 2026-31 Means for You (Jobs, Prices & Economy) Shafy's Weekly' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The tax authority removed super tax for exporters whose income exceeds PKR 500 million and who derive at least 80% of turnover proceeds from exports.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'What Auto Policy 2026-31 Means for You (Jobs, Prices & Economy) Shafy's Weekly' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Interloop more than doubled consolidated net profit to about PKR 12.45 billion from PKR 5.65 billion, lifting earnings per share from PKR 3.96 in FY25 to PKR 9.06, and declared a PKR 2 dividend.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'What Auto Policy 2026-31 Means for You (Jobs, Prices & Economy) Shafy's Weekly' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The Apna Ghar housing scheme is a four-year programme intended to finance loans for around 500,000 homes; roughly 150,000 applications had been received and the government was considering scaling it up.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'What Auto Policy 2026-31 Means for You (Jobs, Prices & Economy) Shafy's Weekly' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: Attacks on tankers and oil facilities around the Strait of Hormuz and the Bab el-Mandeb lift crude prices, which feeds into Pakistani fuel prices, inflation and therefore the policy rate path.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'What Auto Policy 2026-31 Means for You (Jobs, Prices & Economy) Shafy's Weekly' (YouTube transcript, undated)

fact_text: The analyst notes the PSX tends to sell off through weeks of rising oil prices and Middle East escalation, because higher oil means higher inflation and less room for rate cuts in Pakistan.
source_name: Abdul Rehman Najam, 'What Auto Policy 2026-31 Means for You (Jobs, Prices & Economy) Shafy's Weekly' (YouTube transcript, undated)
